title: Grateful Dead Live at Golden Hall on 1970-01-10
lineage: Reel (Akai GX636) -> Apogee Mini-Me (24bit/96k) -> Apogee Mini-Dac -> Wavelab 5 -> FLAC/16

ai_review.summary: Soundboard source with good clarity captures an average Jan ’70 set highlighted by a standout Me & My Uncle and solid Black Peter.
ai_review.review: The Miller 127228 soundboard tape sounds noticeably better than older circulating sources, offering decent balance and image. Musically the show is fairly ordinary for early‑1970, with a few bright spots – an especially lively Me & My Uncle, a strong Black Peter, and the ever‑present Mason’s Children – but it lacks the extended jams that make the era memorable.

ai_rating.rationale: Show quality is average with a few highlights, while the recording is a solid soundboard version; combined weighted score yields ~3.3.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Miller's updated 127228 file is clearer and better balanced than earlier sources (which suffered from image problems and speed issues). No major mudding reported, but the tape still has typical early‑70 quirks.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A fairly routine Jan ’70 performance with no major jam sequences; the set feels like a quick, ‘get‑through‑it’ show rather than a landmark concert.
